subject: general
question: You are an examiner conducting an exam. You doubt that a student is trying to look over into another student's answer sheet. What will you do?

options.text: You will shout loudly so that the student may deter from attempting to copy
You will relocate the student to another desk in the exam room
Tell the nearby students about your doubt and ask them to be careful with their answer sheets
Keep the concerned student under vigilance and verify if your doubt is actually, true

solution:
Shouting loudly will disturb students giving the exam.

Relocating the student based on a doubt is not appropriate. If the examiner is sure that the student is cheating then relocating the student is correct but it should not be done on the basis of a doubt.

Telling the nearby students about my doubt will create a negative impact on the student if the student was not cheating. It should not be done on the basis of a doubt.

Keeping the concerned student under vigilance and verify if your doubt is actually, true is the most preferred course of action.

Hence, ‘**option 4**’ is the correct answer.
